ambiguities.question: What does `goldfish` read when the first hash-matching entry names a different set of repositories (for example a subset) than the packet being opened, with no differing head among the shared ones? Is that `ran_at_head`, `ran_earlier` or `absent`?

`ran_earlier` fires on any head change, including a rebase or unrelated edit. A builder who acts on the questions by amending the criteria changes the hash and reads `absent`, so it is uncounted. A rebase changes the base, so the record name no longer matches and it also reads `absent`. Is 'none reads ran_earlier' meant to prove 'the builder changed nothing after a pre-pass'? If it is, how are these cases handled?
Does 'ten counted reviews in this repository' include reviews whose packet spans several repositories? If it does, which repository does each review belong to?
Skipping the pre-pass is allowed and skipped reviews don't count. What happens if ten counted reviews never accrue? Is there a deadline or fallback for the earn-its-place test?

When the fresh process starts but then fails, times out or returns unusable output, what is the exit code, and is an entry appended? Criterion 2 says it exits 0 whatever the questions say, and criterion 5 covers only a tool that can't start.

The record name carries a single 12-character base, but heads are compared across 'every repository'. For a multi-repository packet, which base names the file, and how are the other repositories' bases matched?
